title: Blender's bmesh operators can return elements in memory order, so exports differ run to run
observation: A headless Blender build of the same assets, run twice with fixed seeds, wrote byte-identical data for 44 of 45 assets; one (extruded paving slabs) came out with its normals, colours and triangles in a different order each run although the geometry was the same. Sorting each piece's vertices by position and its faces by their vertex numbers, and starting each face at its lowest vertex, made every rebuild byte-identical. Blender's FBX writer also embedded the .blend's absolute path (the machine's user folder).
recommendation: When generated art is committed, sort geometry deterministically before writing it, hash two rebuilds to prove it, and scrub absolute paths from exported files (in place, at the same length for FBX's length-prefixed strings).
applies_when: Committing data or files generated by Blender scripts
limits: Blender 4.5.10 LTS on Windows; FBX files still record a creation time

evidence.detail: Section 8: byte-identical rebuilds and no machine path.
